problem: TriOS installed only a status-bar menu and never created the standard application Edit menu. AppKit therefore had no key-equivalent path for Command-V, C, X, A, or Z, and forwarding the events to NSTextView.keyDown was not a reliable substitute.
solution: Installed a standard nil-target Edit menu for responder-chain routing and added an explicit chat-text-view fallback for copy, paste, cut, select all, undo, and redo. Programmatic clear and history replacements now emit text-change notifications so the SwiftUI binding stays synchronized.
lesson: Native macOS editing shortcuts belong to the application menu and responder chain. A custom text view may add a narrow fallback, but it should not replace the standard Edit menu or intercept unrelated input-method events.
